fields.h1: Build a Medical Consent Form for Minor Children While You're Away
fields.product_name: Medical Consent Form for Minor Builder
fields.hero_description: Build a medical consent form for minor children that names the caregiver and the dates, with allergies and insurance attached.
fields.features_heading: What a Caregiver Needs at the Front Desk
fields.features_subheading: Who may consent, for how long, and the health details a nurse asks for first.
fields.feature_1:
The adult named, with a start and end date

Name each adult who may consent to care, with a phone number and their relationship to the child. The form asks when the authorization starts and ends, and the record shows both.
fields.feature_2:
Allergies and medicines at the top

Ask about allergies, daily medicines and ongoing conditions on the first screen. A yes opens a box for the details, and the caregiver reads them first in the child's record.
fields.feature_3:
Both sides of the insurance card

Have the parent photograph the front and back of the child's insurance card. The photos are saved in the same record as the signed form, beside the pediatrician's name and number.
fields.feature_4:
A signature from the parent's phone

The parent types a full name and signs on screen from wherever they are traveling. The app saves the signature with the date and time, and every form sits in a database you own.
fields.feature_5:
An email before the end date

Choose how many days before the end date the parent hears about it. The app sends an email with a link to sign a new form, and it reminds any parent who has not signed the first one.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. An exchange program or a nanny agency can run the form inside its own family portal and keep building on it there.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Gets Named on the Form
fields.tab_content_1:
When Grandma gets to urgent care, the card is on her phone

Claire Ashdown flies out for 10 days and names her parents, Ruth and Harold, to consent to care for her son Emmett, 8. The form lists his peanut allergy and his inhaler. When Emmett splits his chin on a slide, Ruth opens the signed form at urgent care, with both sides of his insurance card.
fields.tab_content_2:
From the lake house, a friend's mom has the details

Lucy Ferraro is 11 and spending 7 days at a lake house with her best friend's family. Her father, Daniel, names Elena Delgado as the adult who may approve Lucy's care that week. He adds the pediatrician's phone and notes no daily medicine. Elena gets the signed form by email before they leave.
fields.tab_content_3:
By the first day of school, 37 of 40 forms are in

Bridgeway Exchange places 40 high school students with host families for the year. Each student's parents sign from their home country to name the host parents. Lena Hartwell, the coordinator, sees 37 of 40 forms signed by the first day of school. The parents of the other 3 students get an email reminder.
fields.tab_content_4:
Into a second year with the nanny, signed 14 days early

Marisol Abrego picks up Finn and Hattie Brack from school every weekday. Their father, Owen, signed a form naming her for their medical care through August 31. The app emails him 14 days before the end date. He signs a new form for the second year from that email, and her record shows the new end date.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable PDFs and hospital sheets: a law office's form to notarize, a hospital's grandparent consent, a vision clinic's parental consent, a state signature form, a site selling minor consent PDFs and a health plan's authorization. Each is a blank page a parent fills in by hand and hands over. None keeps the child's allergies, medicines and insurance card with the signed authorization, none ends on a date, and none tells an exchange program which parents abroad have not signed. This page builds the form a parent signs to name the adult who may consent to care while the parent is away (a grandparent, a friend's family, a host family, a nanny), saved as a record the caregiver opens on a phone. It stays apart from the parent consent page, which is about schools and clubs collecting consent for their own activities.

claims_to_source: California Family Code 6910: a parent, guardian or relative caregiver may authorize in writing an adult into whose care a minor has been entrusted to consent to medical or dental care for the minor

Texas Family Code 32.001(a)(5): an adult who has actual care, control and possession of the child and has written authorization to consent from a person having the right to consent may consent to treatment when that person cannot be contacted
Texas Family Code 32.001(a)(1): a grandparent may consent to a child's treatment when the person with the right to consent cannot be contacted and has not given actual notice to the contrary

Texas Family Code 32.002(a): consent to treatment under the subchapter must be in writing, signed by the person giving consent, and given to the doctor, hospital or other medical facility that administers the treatment
Texas Family Code 32.001(c): the section does not apply to consent for a child's immunization

Texas Family Code 32.002(b): the consent must include the child's name, one or both parents' names if known and any managing conservator or guardian, the consenting person's name and relationship to the child, a statement of the nature of the treatment, and the date treatment is to begin
